check.title: how the server authenticates to its facilitator
check.clause: outside the protocol: x402 does not define facilitator authentication; providers such as the Coinbase facilitator require a signed JWT per call. Decoded, never verified: the signature is not in the trace

findings.detail: no Authorization header on facilitator calls

check.title: the /verify request carries x402Version 2, the client's paymentPayload and the offered paymentRequirements
check.clause: x402-specification-v2.md 7.1: request `{x402Version, paymentPayload, paymentRequirements}`

check.title: the /settle request has the same structure and content as /verify
check.clause: x402-specification-v2.md 7.2: "Request: Same structure as /verify endpoint"

check.title: verify completes before settle starts
check.clause: x402-specification-v2.md 6.1, authorization flow: "verify → resource → settle → respond"

findings.detail: first verify finished Some(2026-09-22T07:50:46.449882Z), first settle started 2026-09-22T07:50:46.541401Z

check.title: the resource executes after verify completed and before settle starts
check.clause: x402-specification-v2.md 6.1: "Read-only verify before the resource executes; funds move only after it completes successfully"

check.title: the settlement outcome reaches the client in PAYMENT-RESPONSE with the facilitator's success, transaction and network
check.clause: x402-specification-v2.md 5.3.1: "the server includes transaction details in the payment response field"; transports-v2/http.md, Settlement Response Delivery

check.title: what the facilitator sent in EXTENSION-RESPONSES never reaches the client
check.clause: x402-specification-v2.md 7.2.1: sidechannel "not part of the JSON response body and not forwarded to buyers"

findings.detail: not forwarded: header absent, marker absent from the body and the receipt

check.title: number of /settle calls for one payment
check.clause: x402-specification-v2.md 7.2 allows several settles per payment; reported as a fact

check.title: a payment the facilitator finds invalid is neither settled nor served
check.clause: x402-specification-v2.md 6.1: "at least one check ... MUST run before the resource executes"; authorization flow settles only after a successful resource

check.title: a payment the facilitator finds invalid does not reach the resource
check.clause: x402-specification-v2.md 6.1: "The resource never executes with nothing checked"

check.title: the facilitator's invalidReason is surfaced to the client
check.clause: x402-specification-v2.md 9: error codes "help clients understand why a payment failed"

check.title: a rejected settlement is a 402 whose PAYMENT-RESPONSE relays success false, errorReason and transaction
check.clause: transports-v2/http.md, Error Handling: Payment Failed 402; Settlement Response Delivery, Example (Failure): 402 with PAYMENT-RESPONSE `{success:false, errorReason, transaction:"", network}`

check.title: a settlement_pending outcome reaches the client with its transaction and network, and is not presented as a success
check.clause: x402-specification-v2.md 9: settlement_pending "MUST carry a non-empty transaction ... and network"; 5.3.2 transaction MUST be non-empty when errorReason is settlement_pending

check.title: a pending settlement does not come with a fresh PAYMENT-REQUIRED inviting a second signature
check.clause: not a spec clause: a client that signs again after a pending outcome may pay twice
check.ambiguity: the spec leaves the server's answer to a pending settlement open beyond the receipt content

check.title: an unreadable settle answer is not presented as a successful settlement
check.clause: transports-v2/http.md, Error Handling: 200 means "Payment verified and settled successfully"; nothing was established here

check.title: a failing resource is not settled
check.clause: x402-specification-v2.md 6.1, authorization flow: "funds move only after it completes successfully"

check.title: the same payment identifier with a different payload is refused with 409 and not settled again
check.clause: extensions/payment_identifier.md, Idempotency Behavior: "Same id, different payload | Return 409 Conflict"
check.ambiguity: the extension lets either the server or the facilitator consume the id; a server that delegates it to the facilitator is not wrong, so the tool warns rather than fails

check.title: when required is true, a payment without an id is answered with 400
check.clause: extensions/payment_identifier.md, Idempotency Behavior: "required: true, no id provided | Return 400 Bad Request"

check.title: a replayed payment whose nonce the facilitator refuses is not presented as a new success
check.clause: schemes/exact/scheme_exact.md: "A consumed primitive MUST produce a settlement failure, never a success"
